methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $5M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.4x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Gallox Semiconductors is a seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Jon McCandless and Debdeep Jena that has raised $5M+. The private semiconductor sector includes 8 identifiable private peers (including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched) and 3 liquid public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Valuation analysis was constrained by data limitations. Stage-progression methodology is applicable: using the $5M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage advancement yields $12M. Peer-median triangulation cannot be reliably applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private comparables meeting minimum sample thresholds (0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage peers identified). Public-comp anchoring is inapplicable because Gallox's revenue is not disclosed; while public semiconductors trade at a 21.4x median P/S, this metric cannot be deployed without the target's top-line figure.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $11M to $14M, centered at $12M. This reflects stage-progression mechanics alone and carries material uncertainty. Key risks include the absence of reliable peer benchmarking at seed stage and the inability to calibrate against public-market multiples. Revenue traction and technical IP differentiation within the broader semiconductor landscape remain critical to narrowing valuation bands at future financings.
